title: As speculation/cognition — faith not surer than proper scientia
source_text: XXXIII. Igitur respectu certitudinis illius, quam speculationis, seu cognitionis diximus, fides non est certior scientia proprie dicta; sed ab illa potius certitudine superatur. Etenim quo major ista certitudo, eo longius ab assensu removet omnem dubitationem. Sed fides dubitationi magis est obnoxia quam scientiae, verbi causa Mathematicae. Nam si quis perceptam habet vim demonstrationis alicujus Geometricae, de conclusione tantisper dubitare non potest. Sed fideli saepe luctandum est cum dubitatione atque diffidentia, quibus fides ejus impetitur.
pass_a_gloss: Therefore with respect to that certainty which we have called of speculation or of cognition, faith is not more certain than science properly so called; but is rather surpassed by that certainty. For the greater that certainty, the farther it removes every doubt from assent. But faith is more liable to doubt than the sciences — for example Mathematics. For if anyone has perceived the force of some Geometric demonstration, he cannot doubt of the conclusion even for a little. But the faithful must often wrestle with doubt and distrust by which his faith is assailed.
pass_b_english: Math demonstration: no momentary doubt; faith often wrestles doubt/distrust.
